newsitem.title: UK: Churchill paid millions to keep Spain out of war.
newsitem.headline: Churchill paid millions to keep Spain out of war.

text.p: Britain's Winston Churchill authorised millions of pounds in bribes to keep Spain out of World War Two, according to papers discovered by a British historian.

David Stafford said the British wartime leader approved payments of 2.5 million pounds (about $100 million in today's terms) to advisers and army commanders of fascist leader General Franco to sway them against supporting a Spanish alliance with Nazi Germany.

"Financial subversion was an integral part of British intelligence," Stafford, a professor at Edinburgh University, told Reuters on Monday. "Churchill understood the levers of power available to him as prime minister and was quite willing to use them."

With Germany winning the war across Europe in 1940, the possible entry of neutral Spain posed a significant threat to Britain's war effort. It would have jeopardised shipping lanes in the Mediterranean.

"The payments were a fairly large amount, but given the stakes and the dangers had Franco actively joined on Hitler's side, then perhaps it wasn't such a large amount," said Stafford, whose book "Churchill and the Secret Service" is due out in October.
Spain ultimately stayed out of the war but the deciding factor was Hitler's waning fortunes rather than financial payments, Stafford said.
"The course of history was ultimately more decisive than money, but we'll never know just how influential the payments were."

Stafford unearthed evidence of the bribes among transcripts of memoranda from the British embassy in New York which outlined the payments and detailed meetings between Churchill and the Secret Service.
